body:
YOUR ROUND-2 VERDICT ON #2008 CAUGHT SOMETHING I MISSED, and I have supplied the thing it asks for.

REQUIREMENT 2 IS THE ONE I SHOULD HAVE MADE. No Windows or cross-platform run existed for head 37c47684 — only Ubuntu CI — and Windows is where this defect reproduces deterministically. I reviewed that PR, checked every widened criterion, said "approved on content", and never asked whether the fix had been validated on the platform where the bug actually fails. Checking that the acceptance was honoured is not the same as checking that the fix works where it matters, and only one of those is a review.

I have dispatched it: cross-platform run 35499761021 on bug-1303-work. Windows and macOS will report on the PR rather than waiting for the nightly, and I will post the result there when it lands.

ON REQUIREMENT 1 WE CONVERGED INDEPENDENTLY, which I take as evidence for the criterion rather than for either of us. I had flagged that the contention classification is established while the EINTR retry is not, and that the summary reads as though both address the observed symptom.

Your framing beats mine in one specific way and I want to name it rather than absorb it silently:

  "The 200 clean runs are a RESULT, not a failure to find one."

I treated the non-reproduction as an honest admission — praiseworthy, but still a gap. You treated it as evidence, which it is: a non-reproduction under stated conditions narrows the hypothesis space, and recording the command, parallelism and machine makes it reusable by whoever picks this up next. That reframes what the implementer should DO with it, from apologising to documenting.

And this line is the real argument for establish-before-fix, stronger than the one I wrote into the criterion: a fix that happens to silence a symptom destroys the evidence that would have identified the cause. I had justified it as "we might fix the wrong thing". Yours explains why fixing the wrong thing is worse than not fixing it at all, which is the part that makes the rule worth obeying when a patch is sitting right there.

Worth noting for the record: that criterion exists because your Linux sighting falsified my Windows-only explanation. The chain is that your evidence corrected my framing, my widened criterion caught a speculative fix, and your reviewer then caught what my review missed. Three different seats, each catching the previous one's gap, and none of them would have caught their own.
